title: Tenant encapsulation certification telemetry and evidence pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a production pipeline that emits per-tenant encapsulation certification bundles for Dedicated capacity: an auditable, cryptographically-anchored evidence chain that proves tenant data was served, stored, and deleted according to residency and retention rules. This ticket implements the runtime hook and the evidence assembler service (fence-reconciler), plus a lightweight telemetry surface in Console for auditors and SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant certification bundle (JSON + signed manifest) generated on snapshot or deletion window and stored in the compliance S3 bucket
Bundles include Merkle-rooted manifest of resources (node ids, volume ids, region tags, retention TTLs), signed with KMS-backed key and optionally timestamped via Sigstore-style notary
Console can export a date-range bundle for any dedicated tenant within 48 hours of request
Automated retention enforcement deletes tenant volumes and emits a deletion-proof event; the deletion is verifiable by rechecking stored manifests
End-to-end synthetic canary validates evidence issuance at 95th percentile latency < 5 minutes for normal load
Runbook + playbook created for compliance audits with example auditor query and verification commands
tasks: Spike: design evidence schema and Merkle manifest format (storage keys, field names, schema version)
Implement fence-reconciler service that subscribes to node/volume lifecycle events and materializes manifests
Integrate KMS signing for manifest signatures and support key rotation metadata in bundles
Retention agent: extend tenant-volume controller to emit deletion-proof events before garbage collect
Build Console telemetry panel (Certifications tab) with bundle list, status, and download link
Add synthetic canary workload and e2e tests; CI job to run replay verification daily
Documentation: Confluence spec, compliance export example, and auditor verification scripts
Operational: S3 lifecycle rules, encryption-at-rest, and TTL enforcement checks
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete — proposed manifest uses canonicalized JSON with ordered fields, includes node_id, volume_id, region, model_variant, retention_ttl, last_access_ts. Draft stored in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Tenant+Encapsulation+Spec

2026-02-25: PoC implementation of fence-reconciler finished (branch: feature/tenant-certifier). PoC produces signed bundles and stores them in compliance-s3-bucket. GitHub PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1725
2026-02-28: Infra review — added requirement to support compact binary merkle proof file alongside JSON for large manifests (SSTable-friendly); flagged S3 path partitioning to avoid hot prefixes
2026-03-01: Canary plan drafted — will run 5 synthetic tenants for 24h, assert proof issuance latency and deletion-proof replay accuracy
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee) requested explicit schema versioning and backwards-compatible header in every bundle to support future validators
Security (Maya Chen) asked for HSM-backed signing or at minimum KMS with rotation windows and audit trail; also requested PII redaction guidance for manifests
Design (Ivy Ng) suggested Console export CSV + auditor-friendly PDF summary in addition to JSON bundles
SRE (Omar Singh) recommended adding an async retry queue for reconciler writes with DLQ and operator alerting when bundle write fails > 3 times
open_risks_and_tradeoffs: Storing full manifests for high-churn tenants may be costly; tradeoff: keep compact merkle proofs + manifest snapshots at daily intervals to reduce storage

Strong cryptographic proofs (Sigstore anchoring or external notarization) adds complexity and external dependency; initial rollout will support KMS signatures and optional external timestamping as a post-commit step

Retention enforcement strong consistency vs eventual: immediate deletion-proof semantics require tight coupling to GC path — we'll implement an 'emit-before-delete' contract to get verifiable events without blocking GC for long
Auditor UX: exporting large historical ranges could be slow; we will provide pre-signed archive bundles and async export jobs with email/webhook notifications
deployment_and_rollback: Deploy fence-reconciler in canary region on Dedicated staging tenant fleet first
Feature-flag evidence writes; start with 'write-only' mode where bundles generated but not surfaced in Console
Monitor errors and bundle size distribution for 72h before enabling Console export
Rollback plan: disable reconciler consumers and fallback to daily snapshot job that generates best-effort bundles
operational_runbook_links: Playbook: Auditor Verification Steps — includes example verification script and merkle proof validator: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/auditor-exports
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest canonicalization and signature verification
Integration tests for fence-reconciler -> S3 write path with mock KMS
E2E replay tests: given a date-range bundle, replay resources and assert cohort membership matches recorded events
Performance: synthetic canary with 5 tenants under burst load to validate 95th percentile issuance latency < 5 minutes
